newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Chinese premier not quite illustrious Caracas son.
newsitem.headline: Chinese premier not quite illustrious Caracas son.

text.p: Visiting Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng lost his chance to become "Caracas' Illustrious Son" on Thursday after protesting street vendors forced the cancellation of a ceremony in the Venezuelan city's historic central square.
Li, who was ending a three-nation Latin American tour in Venezuela, was to receive the keys to the nation's capital and the honorific title in leafy Plaza Bolivar.
But Chinese security decided to call the event off after about 40 to 50 street peddlers, wandering salesmen and stall holders gathered in the square in protest over a recent ban on street peddling.
"I don't understand why a protest of 40 people provoked his decision," Caracas mayor Antonio Ledezma, who initiated the ban, told Reuters.
"Especially as Li Peng has faced demonstrations, such as Tiananmen Square," he added. The Town Hall faces the square.
A student-led campaign for democracy centred in Beijing's Tiananmen square was crushed by the Chinese army in June 1989 resulting in loss of life.
